newsitem.title: UK: BBC infringed Barclay brothers' privacy.
newsitem.headline: BBC infringed Barclay brothers' privacy.

text.p: The British Broadcasting Corporation infringed the privacy of newspaper owners David and Frederick Barclay, the Broadcasting Complaints Commission said on Tuesday.

The brothers, who own the Ritz hotel and have extensive media interests, including The European and The Scotsman newspapers, took action after a journalist landed on their private island of Brecqhou, in the Channel Islands, in 1995.
Reporter John Sweeney made the trip even though the Barclays had declined to be interviewed and had refused permission for the visit, the commission said.
The commission rejected the BBC's claim that Sweeney's trip was in the public interest.
David Barclay said: "This is a victory against unwarranted invasion of privacy and television distortion."
The commission also partly upheld a complaint against the BBC by Charles Garside, editor of The European, saying an interview with him had been unfairly edited.
